title: Shortlist Fidelity Matrix and Exercise Rotation Catalog
body:
Purpose
This is a working artifact for improving shortlist quality and standardizing which take-home / live exercises we rotate for different engineering tracks. Goal: reduce time-to-offer, improve signal-to-noise (fewer false positives/negatives), and make interviewer workload predictable. Use as a cookbook for recruiters + interviewers when assembling slate and prepping hiring managers.

Quick notes (TL;DR)
- Matrix ranks candidates on 5 fidelity axes (domain, product, craft, communication, growth bias).
- For each role family we recommend 2 primary exercises (one short live coding + one take-home or design prompt) and 1 fallback.
- We include minimal day-1 onboarding checklist tailored to hire type (IC vs contractor vs manager).
- This doc purposely keeps low friction: exercise durations 30–90 minutes; grading rubric anchored to behavioral evidence not just correctness.

Context / why now
Hiring volume increased into Dedicated and Private product lanes; recruiters report many resumes convert to screen but fail on domain-specific signals later. Current backlog: inconsistent exercises across panels, and repeated take-home requests causing dropout. Need a compact decision framework to: prioritize predictive signals early, set consistent candidate expectations, and unify scoring language across interviewers.

Matrix (at-a-glance) - how to score shortlist candidates before sending exercises
(Use 1–5 scale per axis; rounded to nearest 0.5)
- Domain familiarity: direct product or infra background (examples: model serving, KV cache ops, quantization).
- Product impact orientation: track record of shipping, trade-off thinking, metrics awareness.
- Core craft: algorithmic/engineering fundamentals for role (latency optimization, system design, API design).
- Communicates intent: clarity in PRs, RFCs, stakeholder syncs.
- Growth bias / learnability: evidence candidate learns quickly (side projects, migrations, postmortems).

Scoring guidance:
- 4.0+ : strong fit for phone-screen -> expedited on-site; consider manager loop earlier.
- 3.0–3.9: send one focused exercise (live 40m + short take-home).
- <3.0: optional rescue calls for borderline high potential; otherwise deprioritize.

Exercise rotation catalog (recommended by role family)
Engineering - Backend / Serving Runtime
- Primary: 40m live exercise (pairing) focused on streaming token generation: build simplified generator with attention to incremental output, measure latency for 100k tokens simulated input. Grading rubric: correctness (30%), latency-awareness & tradeoffs (30%), code clarity & decomposition (20%), communication (20%).
- Secondary (take-home, 4–6 hours): design a cache invalidation strategy for prefix/KV caching across replica pools. Ask for diagram, API sketch, and short failure scenarios. Grade on architecture clarity, failure modes, and testability.
- Fallback: design-lite prompt (90m) to sketch a rollout strategy for a new quantized model variant.

Engineering - Infra / SRE
- Primary: incident postmortem simulation (30m live): given a degraded serving-region, ask candidate to triage, propose quick mitigation, and timeline to restore. Grade on prioritization (40%), monitoring signals used (30%), clear escalation & rollback plan (30%).
- Secondary: short script exercise (2 hours) to implement health-check orchestration and graceful drain.

Applied ML / Model Ops
- Primary: model-behavior analysis exercise (60m): small prompt set + outputs; ask candidate to detect regressions, propose evaluation metrics and mitigation plan. Grade: signal detection (35%), metric design (30%), operational path (35%).
- Secondary: take-home for 6 hours to propose quantization profile and expected throughput tradeoffs for specific hardware.

Product / PM (technical)
- Primary: 45m case: rollout plan for a hosted API change impacting latency. Score on user impact mapping (30%), metrics & SLO definitions (30%), migration & communication plan (25%), open risks (15%).

Interview rubric (unified language)
- Evidence-first language: ask for concrete examples and artifacts. Avoid hypotheticals without constraints.
- Use behavioral anchors in each grade band (ex: 3 = "has done this once with help"; 4 = "owns this area and taught others"; 5 = "thought leader, multiple cycles").
- Always capture 2–3 candidate quotes or paraphrases to justify the score.

Scoring template (what interviewer puts in notes)
- Summary (1–2 sentences)
- Top 3 strengths (bulleted)
- Top 3 risks / unknowns
- Score per axis (domain, product, craft, comms, growth) + overall recommend: yes/conditional/no
- Suggested next step (exercise, hire manager call, skip)

Day 1 / first-week ops checklist (for hiring manager / people ops handoff)
- Pre-first-day: invite to onboarding Slack, hardware access request sent, welcome doc + team reading list shared.
- Day 0: create account, set up 1:1 with manager for week 1, calendar blocks for onboarding sessions.
- Day 1 morning: orientation (30m), security review (15m), infra access baseline (2h).
- Week 1: assign mentor, first small ticket (~4–8h), book stakeholder intros.
- Probation evidence to collect by week 8: at least 1 production PR, one cross-team sync led, and performance calibration note from manager.

Manager handoff template (for recruiter to send with offer)
- Short bio of hiring manager, 3 key success metrics for role, top 2 immediate projects, names of mentor and onboarding buddy, expected 30/60/90 deliverables.

Operational guards & constraints
- Max take-home duration: 6 hours. Provide candidate explicit deadline and scoring expectations.
- Live exercise window: 30–90 minutes only. Avoid multi-stage live blocks >2 hrs.
- Reuse of exercises: rotate catalog quarterly to reduce cheating surface. Keep core prompts but change dataset/seed.

Examples of interviewer phrasing (cheap win)
- "Tell me about the last time you shipped a change that reduced p50 latency by >10%. What was your approach?"
- "Walk me through a postmortem you authored; what did you learn and what changed as a result?"

Unresolved questions / TODOs
- Can we get engineering leads to sign off on the primary infra exercise by next sprint? (assign: Ben)
- Need a short-FAQ page for candidates on expected exercise time & tooling; add to confluence (owner: Sonia).
- Split-test whether offering paid take-homes reduces dropout for Senior/Staff candidates. (Jamal to run pilot)

Notes to self / style points
- Keep exercises realistic and close to day-to-day problem. Candidates value signal over toy puzzles.
- Emphasize communication and tradeoffs; a perfect implementation is less predictive than thoughtfulness in infra decisions.

References
- Link to current shortlist tracker (JIRA-PEOPLE-1423).
- Slack: #recruiting-ops, #eng-hiring.

Revision history
